title: Cisco Turns Its Attention To The Control Layers Of Its Quantum Network
gist: Cisco's Outshift unit unveiled a Quantum Network Controller research prototype and a Network-Aware Quantum Compiler to automate entanglement distribution across multi-vendor quantum systems, arguing quantum must scale out via networking. Cisco puts interconnected quantum systems three to five years away, with transduction and quantum memory unsolved.

insights.claim: Cisco argues quantum scaling requires connecting separate quantum computers into distributed, cloud-like architectures, scaling out as classical computing did, not just building larger single systems with more qubits.
insights.speaker: Jeff Burt
insights.so_what: Positions networking vendors as a necessary layer of the quantum stack rather than bystanders to qubit-count races.
insights.locator: In short, it is about scaling out

insights.claim: Point-to-point wiring does not scale: connecting 1,000 quantum nodes point to point takes close to 500,000 dedicated links, which motivates a switched any-to-any fabric with automated control.
insights.speaker: Vijoy Pandey
insights.so_what: Arithmetic case for quantum switching and control-plane products.
insights.quote: Connecting 1,000 quantum nodes point to point takes close to 500,000 dedicated links

insights.claim: Quantum networks today are manually stitched and configured point to point; once application requests to entangle nodes arrive at machine speed, human configuration cannot keep up, so a machine-speed control plane is required.
insights.speaker: Ramana Kompella
insights.so_what: The missing control layer is the stated bottleneck for useful quantum networks.
insights.quote: human way of configuring and reconfiguring the fabric is not going to scale

insights.claim: Cisco's quantum stack so far: Outshift put in charge early 2025, a prototype entangling chip generating entangled photon pairs over distance in late 2025, a Universal Quantum Switch prototype in April 2026 linking different vendors and modalities (superconducting, photonics, neutral atoms, trapped ions), and now the Quantum Network Controller.
insights.speaker: Jeff Burt
insights.so_what: Cisco is assembling an end-to-end quantum networking roadmap, all still research prototypes, not products.
insights.locator: Early last year, the Outshift group

insights.claim: The Quantum Network Controller offers 'Entanglement-as-a-Service': applications request entanglement specifying endpoints, fidelity, rate and timing through an API over switches, detectors and timing systems, and the controller schedules links, tunes them, and retries or reinitializes on degradation.
insights.speaker: Jeff Burt
insights.so_what: An abstraction layer like this would let developers consume quantum links as a service, analogous to cloud networking.
insights.locator: Cisco's controller does this by acting as an abstraction layer

insights.claim: Quantum controllers are harder than classical ones because quantum operations are probabilistic with short coherence times, and loss, fidelity, synchronization and system performance determine whether an operation succeeds, unlike deterministic classical scheduling.
insights.speaker: Reza Nejabati
insights.so_what: Explains why classical SDN tooling cannot simply be reused, protecting a niche for specialized control software.

insights.claim: Cisco's Network-Aware Quantum Compiler splits a large circuit into smaller pieces and has the controller distribute entanglement at the right time so partial computed state moves between processors; the compiler determines needed entanglement, nodes and fidelity, and the controller executes it on the network.
insights.speaker: Ramana Kompella
insights.so_what: Distributed quantum computing becomes an application-layer problem, giving compiler and orchestration software a role.
insights.locator: The first application that we tackle

insights.claim: Cisco intends to be multi-vendor, saying it will not build everything itself and the controller must hide the complexity of onboarding many different devices; its own modality of choice, like IBM, is superconducting.
insights.speaker: Ramana Kompella
insights.so_what: Vendor-neutral control layer is a standards-style play; watch partnerships with qubit makers.
insights.quote: We would love to think that everything will be built by Cisco

insights.claim: Quantum networking market is estimated around $2 billion, with players including Nu Quantum, Photonics Inc., Aliro Technologies, QphoX and Qunnect, which Cisco partnered with to demonstrate entanglement swapping over 17.6 km of New York City telecom fiber.
insights.speaker: Jeff Burt
insights.so_what: Small but crowded early field; Cisco partnerships give a read on who may be acquired or integrated.

insights.claim: Quantum networking has classical near-term uses: instant-communication 'decision coordination' for high-speed trading between separated nodes (Cisco Quantum Sync), and eavesdropper detection by mixing entangled photons with classical ones on the same fiber, since an interceptor disturbs entanglement.
insights.speaker: Ramana Kompella
insights.so_what: Finance and security are the plausible first paying customers before quantum computing networks mature.
insights.locator: Kompella notes that quantum use cases

insights.claim: Kompella says interconnected quantum systems could appear in three to five years, gated by transduction (converting quantum information between physical domains while preserving superposition and entanglement) and by nascent quantum memory needed to improve fidelity and timing.
insights.speaker: Ramana Kompella
insights.so_what: Transduction and quantum memory are the technical milestones to monitor before revenue-scale quantum networking.
insights.locator: The development of quantum networks is still in the early phases
